macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks suffer sharp weekly decline as oil and AI concerns weigh
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.09% on Friday to 7,659.42, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.14% to 26,140.03, and the Dow declined 0.34% to 52,001.70. The S&P 500 lost 1.9% for the week, while the Nasdaq fell about 4.5% as rising crude prices and concerns about the AI trade pressured technology and semiconductor shares.

items.title: Oil prices surge toward $110 as inflation fears intensify
items.summary: Brent crude settled at $109.86 per barrel, up 3.72%, while U.S. crude rose 3.51% to $101.41. The spike renewed concerns that higher energy costs could complicate inflation progress and monetary-policy decisions.

items.title: Fed enters blackout period ahead of October policy meeting
items.summary: Federal Reserve officials are scheduled to enter their communications blackout before the October 27–28 policy meeting. Markets reduced expectations for a rate hike after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh did not indicate that rates would need to rise, while emphasizing the central bank’s policy independence and commitment to price stability.

items.title: AI and semiconductor shares lead market selloff
items.summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 11.4% for the week, its longest losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis. CoreWeave, SK Hynix, Arm, SanDisk, Oracle and Tesla were among the major technology-related decliners on Friday.

items.title: Investors turn to major technology earnings
items.summary: Tesla, Meta Platforms and Procter & Gamble are scheduled to report in the coming week, followed by Microsoft and Amazon later in the month. Analysts expect strong third-quarter earnings growth, supported by technology companies and continued artificial-intelligence investment, although Tesla is expected to face pressure on profits and higher capital spending.

items.title: Exxon expects refining margins to boost third-quarter earnings
items.summary: Exxon is expected to receive a roughly $4.5 billion contribution to third-quarter earnings from higher refining margins, highlighting the earnings impact of elevated energy-market volatility.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin stabilizes near $82,000 as crypto market remains volatile
items.summary: Bitcoin rebounded above $82,000 after briefly falling below $80,000, while analysts watched resistance near $84,000. Ether slipped below $2,400, down 1.36% over 24 hours, and total crypto liquidations reached about $222 million, mostly affecting long positions.

items.title: Celestia token rises 57% amid Eden chain launch
items.summary: Celestia’s TIA gained 57% over the week to about $0.75, its highest level since November 2025, following the launch of Eden, an EVM-compatible chain focused on AI-agent experimentation.

items.title: Judge leaves Gemini’s $5 million CFTC settlement intact
items.summary: A federal judge rejected a joint request from Gemini and the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission to undo a $5 million consent judgment, leaving the permanent injunction in place.

items.title: Bitcoin mining difficulty reaches highest level since March 2023
items.summary: Bitcoin mining difficulty rose 5.92% to a new high for the period, increasing competitive and operational pressure on miners.

items.title: Crypto investment products see continued outflows
items.summary: Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded approximately $134.56 million in net outflows over seven days, while Ether ETFs saw about $293.85 million in outflows.

items.title: EU crypto platforms ordered to wind down non-MiCA operations
items.summary: European crypto platforms were reportedly ordered to discontinue services that do not comply with the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets framework, increasing pressure on firms to obtain or operate under the required authorization.

items.title: Solana prepares Alpenglow consensus upgrade
items.summary: Solana’s Alpenglow consensus upgrade is scheduled to reach mainnet-beta around October 21 and is designed to replace TowerBFT while targeting roughly 150-millisecond finality.

items.title: European banks-backed Qivalis receives e-money license
items.summary: Qivalis, backed by 37 European banks, received an e-money license from De Nederlandsche Bank and plans to issue a euro stablecoin under MiCA within months.

items.title: Aptos activates encrypted mempool and Confidential APT
items.summary: Aptos made its opt-in Encrypted Mempool and Confidential APT features live on mainnet, aiming to encrypt pending transactions until block finalization and reduce maximal extractable value risks.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta releases open-weight Muse Spark AI model
items.summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts model activating about 42 billion parameters per token. The model is aimed at coding and AI-agent workloads and reportedly supports context windows of up to one million tokens.[1][2]
items.source: Latent Space / The AI Daily Digest

items.title: DeepSeek updates V4.1 Flash
items.summary: DeepSeek moved its V4.1 Flash service to the V4.1-Flash-1017 snapshot, reporting gains across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks and visual benchmarks. The update is available through DeepSeek’s web, mobile and API products.[2][6]

items.title: Microsoft completes pretraining of MAI-Base-2
items.summary: Microsoft said it completed pretraining MAI-Base-2, a large mixture-of-experts base model with roughly 2.8 trillion total and 80 billion active parameters. The company reported training it for 38 days on 6,000 Nvidia GB200 GPUs.[2]

items.title: Mistral previews trillion-parameter Large 4 model
items.summary: Mistral previewed Large 4, an open-weight model designed for coding, autonomous agents and multimodal workloads, and said it plans to release the weights soon.[2]

items.title: Anthropic expands external oversight of AI models
items.summary: Anthropic granted six evaluators from the nonprofit METR employee-level access to inspect its models. The move follows growing concern about AI agents behaving beyond intended instructions.[4][7]
items.source: The AI Daily Digest / Economic Times

items.title: OpenAI adds browser interaction to ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI announced that ChatGPT can read users’ open Chrome tabs and, with additional setup, perform actions such as filling forms, sending messages, downloading files and organizing tabs.[4]

items.title: Researchers release MLExpert agentic machine-learning model
items.summary: Researchers from Shanghai AI Lab introduced MLExpert, a 35-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts system for autonomous machine-learning engineering. The reported system substantially improved performance on MLE-Bench Lite through agentic training and reinforcement-learning techniques.[8]

items.title: Google DeepMind agents complete Minecraft autonomously
items.summary: A team of four Gemini 4 Argon agents reportedly completed Minecraft in 27 hours and 14 minutes without human assistance. The agents coordinated roles, recovered from hundreds of deaths and wrote and debugged thousands of programs before defeating the Ender Dragon.[8]

items.title: Nvidia releases new open multimodal models
items.summary: Nvidia released new Nemotron models, including Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120-billion-parameter open multimodal model designed for always-on agents.[4][9]
items.source: The AI Daily Digest / Israel Hayom

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Indie developer cancels public demo over AI-copying concerns
items.summary: The developers of Drunken Goddess Reflux canceled a planned public demo, citing concerns that generative AI could enable rapid cloning of the game. They will instead hold closed sessions for a limited group of participants.

items.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy demo announced for PlayStation Plus Premium
items.summary: A free demo for Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is scheduled for October 20, alongside a trial for Mortal Shell II, for PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers.

items.title: Boltgun 2 launches on PC and current-generation consoles
items.summary: Boltgun 2 released October 14 for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox at $24.99. A Switch 2 version is planned for a later date.

items.title: No Man’s Sky expands to iPhone and iPad
items.summary: Hello Games announced that No Man’s Sky will arrive on iPhone and iPad on October 28, bringing the space-exploration game to additional mobile platforms.

items.title: Forza Horizon 6 PlayStation 5 release delayed
items.summary: Playground Games reportedly delayed the PlayStation 5 version of Forza Horizon 6 from 2026 to January 26, 2027.
